newsitem.title: UK: Viglen says Sugar not to cut stake now.
newsitem.headline: Viglen says Sugar not to cut stake now.

text.p: Viglen Technology Plc, the new-listed company born out of reorganisation of electronics group Amstrad Plc said on Monday that Alan Sugar would not reduce his current stake in the company for the time being.

Viglen, which made its market debut on Monday and was traded at 64 1/2 pence said Sugar, former Amstrad chief, had taken the decision as he felt the company's current rating did not reflect the underlying value of Viglen's business.
The company's previous valuations had pegged the stock at around 70 pence.

The restructuring of Amstrad and its reincarnation as Viglen was announced in June. Amstrad shareholders received one Viglen share plus a share of Amstrad's Betacom unit, a share in proceeds of litigation over disc drive faults and 163 pence in loan notes.
